headings.title: Creation and responsibilities of the division
headings.reviewNote: Creates the Division of Comprehensive Psychiatric Services within the department to supervise and oversee facilities and services.

headings.title: Powers, functions, and duties of the division
headings.reviewNote: Enumerates twelve specific powers, functions, and duties of the division regarding planning, research, standards, and funding.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 632.010 establishing the Division of Comprehensive Psychiatric Services and specifying its twelve statutory duties (L. 1980 H.B. 1724).

headings.title: Advisory council role and membership size
headings.reviewNote: Designates the Missouri advisory council for comprehensive psychiatric services to advise the division with up to twenty-five members.

headings.title: Council appointments, terms, and composition requirements
headings.reviewNote: Governs director appointments, three-year overlapping terms, organizational representation, and vendor membership limits.

headings.title: Filling of council vacancies by director
headings.reviewNote: Directs that vacancies occurring on the advisory council are filled by appointment of the director.

headings.title: Meetings and election of council chairman
headings.reviewNote: Requires meetings at least every ninety days at the call of the division director or the council chairman elected by the council.

headings.title: Reimbursement of reasonable and necessary expenses
headings.reviewNote: Requires reimbursement of each member's reasonable and necessary expenses, including travel expenses under department employee regulations, incurred in performing official duties.

headings.title: Subcouncils and study and recommendation duties
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes division of the council into subcouncils and tasks it with studying and planning mental disorder services.

headings.title: Conflict of interest restrictions and member removal
headings.reviewNote: Bars members from participating in decisions involving personal interest or income and establishes removal grounds.

headings.title: State plan collaboration and advisory responsibilities
headings.reviewNote: Specifies council state-plan collaboration and advisory duties including meetings, technology review, service delivery recommendations, funding/licensing standards, and suicide prevention oversight.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 8 subsection headings for 632.020 detailing the Missouri advisory council for comprehensive psychiatric services structure, terms, quarterly meetings, expense reimbursement, ethics, and duties including suicide prevention oversight (L. 1980 H.B. 1724, A.L. 2011 H.B. 464).

headings.title: Preparation and annual revision of state plan
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department to prepare and annually revise a coordinated state plan for comprehensive psychiatric services.

headings.title: Mandatory contents and elements of state plan
headings.reviewNote: Specifies required components of the state plan including needs assessments, goals, inventories, evaluations, and rules.

headings.title: Consideration of regional plans in preparation
headings.reviewNote: Mandates that the department take regional plans into consideration when preparing the statewide plan.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsection headings for 632.030 governing preparation, annual revision, mandatory contents, and regional plan consideration for the comprehensive psychiatric services state plan (L. 1980 H.B. 1724).

headings.title: Establishment and appointment of regional advisory councils
headings.reviewNote: Permits the department director to establish regional councils and requires the division director to appoint up to twenty regional residents for staggered three-year terms.

headings.title: Consumer representation and vendor membership limitations
headings.reviewNote: Mandates at least one-half consumer representation and limits vendor participation to no more than one-fourth.

headings.title: Conflict of interest prohibition and removal grounds
headings.reviewNote: Bars regional members from participating in decisions involving personal interest or income and authorizes removal.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsection headings for 632.040 authorizing regional advisory councils, consumer/vendor composition limits, and conflict of interest restrictions (L. 1980 H.B. 1724).

headings.title: Participation and contents of regional plans
headings.reviewNote: Requires regional councils to participate in preparing, reviewing, and recommending regional plans with inventories and goals.

headings.title: Appropriations condition for regional council staff
headings.reviewNote: Mandates that any regional advisory council staff shall be provided only from funds appropriated specifically for that purpose, effective July 1, 1981.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 632.045 establishing regional plan participation/contents and staff appropriation condition (L. 1980 H.B. 1724; footnote notes subsection 2 effective 7-01-81).

headings.title: Adult voluntary application and outpatient evaluation
headings.reviewNote: Directs acceptance of adult voluntary admission applications for outpatient evaluation subject to suitable accommodations.

headings.title: Inpatient admission criteria for diagnosed mental disorders
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes private and requires public inpatient admission if diagnosed with a mental disorder and accommodations are available.

headings.title: Patient rights and informed consent to treatment
headings.reviewNote: Establishes voluntary patient status and informed consent rights for treatment and medication except in emergencies.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsection headings for 632.105 governing adult voluntary admission applications, inpatient criteria, and voluntary patient informed consent rights (L. 1980 H.B. 1724, A.L. 2011 H.B. 555 merged with H.B. 648).

headings.title: Minor voluntary application and outpatient evaluation
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes parent or legal custodian to apply for voluntary admission and outpatient evaluation of a minor.

headings.title: Minor inpatient admission criteria for mental disorders
headings.reviewNote: Governs private and public inpatient admission of a minor diagnosed with a mental disorder and suitable for treatment.

headings.title: Parental consent and medication refusal rights
headings.reviewNote: Vests parent or legal custodian with authority to consent to treatment and refuse medication except in emergencies.

headings.title: Peace officer custody and evaluation transport
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes parent or legal custodian to request a peace officer to take a minor into custody for facility evaluation.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 subsection headings for 632.110 governing minor voluntary admission applications, inpatient criteria, parental consent/refusal rights, and peace officer transport (L. 1980 H.B. 1724, A.L. 2011 H.B. 555 merged with H.B. 648).

headings.title: Guardian application and outpatient evaluation of ward
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes guardian of an incapacitated person to apply for voluntary admission and outpatient evaluation.

headings.title: Inpatient admission criteria for diagnosed ward
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes private and requires public inpatient admission of diagnosed incapacitated ward for up to thirty days.

headings.title: Court authorization for continued inpatient hospitalization
headings.reviewNote: Requires court authorization for guardian to continue inpatient hospitalization and consent to continued treatment.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsection headings for 632.120 governing guardian voluntary admission of incapacitated persons, 30-day inpatient evaluation, and court authorization for continued hospitalization (L. 1980 H.B. 1724 through A.L. 2011 H.B. 555 merged with H.B. 648).

headings.title: Adult voluntary patient release request and refusal
headings.reviewNote: Requires immediate release upon oral or written request unless the facility head determines likelihood of serious physical harm.

headings.title: Involuntary detention application upon release refusal
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes continued detention following release refusal only if an application for involuntary detention is completed.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 632.150 governing adult voluntary patient release requests, refusal for serious physical harm risk, and involuntary detention application (L. 1980 H.B. 1724, A.L. 2023 S.B. 106).

headings.title: Minor voluntary patient release request and conditions
headings.reviewNote: Requires release of minor upon request of minor, parent, or custodian, conditioned on consent of original applicant.

headings.title: Involuntary detention application upon minor release refusal
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes detention refusal for serious harm risk only if an involuntary detention or chapter 211 proceeding is initiated.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 632.155 governing minor voluntary patient release requests, applicant consent condition, and involuntary detention or chapter 211 refusal procedure (L. 1980 H.B. 1724, A.L. 2023 S.B. 106).

headings.title: Periodic one hundred eighty-day review and discharge
headings.reviewNote: Requires facility head to review patient condition every one hundred eighty days to determine need for hospitalization.

headings.title: Care in least restrictive environment review
headings.reviewNote: Requires facility head to verify that the patient is receiving care and treatment in the least restrictive environment.

headings.title: Transmittal of review and plan to guardian
headings.reviewNote: Requires copies of the periodic review and individualized treatment plan to be sent to the guardian and the court.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsection headings for 632.175 establishing 180-day patient condition reviews, least restrictive environment verification, and guardian/court reporting (L. 1980 H.B. 1724).

headings.title: Application for ninety-six-hour emergency detention
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes any adult person to file a sworn court application alleging mental disorder and likelihood of serious harm.

headings.title: Ex parte court review, probable cause, and warrant
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes ex parte court finding of probable cause and issuance of peace officer transport order for ninety-six-hour detention.

headings.title: Peace officer emergency custody without prior warrant
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes peace officers to take persons into emergency custody upon reasonable cause of imminent serious harm.

headings.title: Facility professional application for ninety-six-hour detention
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes facility physicians, nurses, or mental health professionals to complete emergency detention applications.

headings.title: Exemption from notarization under penalty of perjury
headings.reviewNote: Exempts applications by officers, medical staff, and hospital employees from notarization pursuant to section 492.060.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 5 subsection headings for 632.305 governing adult, ex parte court, peace officer, and facility professional 96-hour emergency detention applications and section 492.060 notarization exemptions (L. 1980 H.B. 1724 through A.L. 2026 H.B. 2372 merged with H.B. 2637 & 3155; severability § 1.1005).

headings.title: Provisional acceptance of court and professional applications
headings.reviewNote: Directs mandatory public and permissive private acceptance of respondents under court order or medical application.

headings.title: Discretionary acceptance of peace officer applications
headings.reviewNote: Provides that mental health facilities may, but are not required to, accept applications and respondents from peace officers.

headings.title: Transportation requirement upon rejection of admission
headings.reviewNote: Requires facility or transporting agency to provide immediate return transportation if admission is refused.

headings.title: Catchment area contracts for substance abuse disorders
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes department contracts requiring catchment area providers to accept and evaluate substance abuse respondents.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 subsection headings for 632.310 governing provisional acceptance of court/professional and peace officer applications, return transportation upon rejection, and catchment area substance abuse contracts (L. 1980 H.B. 1724 through A.L. 2023 S.B. 106).

headings.title: Three-hour intake examination, notices, and attorney access
headings.reviewNote: Requires professional examination, service of application and rights notice, and attorney contact assistance within three hours.

headings.title: Eighteen-hour examination by licensed physician
headings.reviewNote: Mandates that the respondent be examined by a licensed physician within eighteen hours after facility arrival.

headings.title: Forty-eight-hour statutory rights explanation
headings.reviewNote: Requires facility staff to meet with the respondent within forty-eight hours to explain statutory rights under this chapter.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsection headings for 632.320 establishing mandatory 3-hour, 18-hour, and 48-hour intake examination and rights procedures (L. 1980 H.B. 1724, A.L. 2023 S.B. 106).

headings.title: Detention extension pending twenty-one-day or outpatient petition
headings.reviewNote: Permits detention for an additional two judicial days if a petition for twenty-one-day or outpatient treatment is filed.

headings.title: Petition filing deadlines, grounds, and contents
headings.reviewNote: Permits filing a 21-day inpatient or up to 180-day outpatient petition within 96 hours, requires court service of the petition and witness list at least 24 hours before hearing, and specifies nine mandatory allegations and verification.

headings.title: Consideration of chapter 475 guardianship or conservatorship
headings.reviewNote: Requires the petitioner to consider whether the respondent meets chapter 475 criteria for a full or limited guardian or conservator and, if so, to proceed under subsection 4.

headings.title: Chapter 475 guardianship petition and emergency detention
headings.reviewNote: Directs the facility head believing a respondent may be incapacitated or disabled to file a chapter 475 petition and seek temporary emergency detention under section 475.355 if appropriate, with a hearing within two judicial days and preservation of chapter 632 proceedings if denied.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 subsection headings for 632.330 (rewrote fabricated subsections 3 and 4) covering two-judicial-day extension, 21-day inpatient / 180-day outpatient petition contents and 24-hour service, consideration of chapter 475 guardianship/conservatorship, and chapter 475 petition/emergency detention procedures (L. 1980 H.B. 1724 through A.L. 2023 S.B. 106).

headings.title: Hearing schedule, notice, and continuance standards
headings.reviewNote: Sets hearing within two judicial days of petition filing, requires prompt notice, and restricts continuances to good cause.

headings.title: Hearing conduct and procedural rights of respondent
headings.reviewNote: Requires informal hearing setting and enumerates respondent procedural rights including counsel, evidence, and cross-examination.

headings.title: Requirement and exceptions for respondent presence
headings.reviewNote: Mandates respondent presence at the hearing unless excused due to physical incapacity or disruptive courtroom conduct.

headings.title: Clear and convincing standard for detention order
headings.reviewNote: Directs court to order least restrictive detention for up to twenty-one inpatient or one hundred eighty outpatient days.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 subsection headings for 632.335 establishing 21-day inpatient / 180-day outpatient hearing schedule, respondent procedural rights (including jury request), presence exceptions, and clear and convincing detention standard (L. 1980 H.B. 1724 through A.L. 2023 S.B. 106).

headings.title: Immediate ninety-six-hour detention during outpatient order
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes a supervisory mental health program during a 180-day outpatient order to direct up to 96 hours of immediate inpatient detention and sheriff transport upon good cause of serious harm, with longer detention governed by section 632.330.

headings.title: Evidentiary use of ninety-six-hour outpatient detentions
headings.reviewNote: Permits the court to consider evidence of 96-hour detentions during a 180-day outpatient detention period when determining additional periods of detention and treatment.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 632.337 (rewrote both fabricated subsections) covering immediate 96-hour inpatient detention and sheriff transport during 180-day court-ordered outpatient detention, and evidentiary use of 96-hour detentions in subsequent proceedings (L. 1996 S.B. 884 & 841).

headings.title: Additional ninety-day detention order criteria
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the court after hearing to order up to 90 additional inpatient days or up to 180 outpatient days before expiration of a 21-day inpatient order if likelihood of serious harm continues.

headings.title: Ninety-day petition filing timelines and contents
headings.reviewNote: Directs the program head, if reasonable cause exists within seventeen days of the section 632.335 hearing, to file a 90-day inpatient or 180-day outpatient petition with an individualized treatment plan, setting a hearing within four judicial days and service within two judicial days.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 632.340 (corrected subsection 2 filing deadline from 15 days to within 17 days of the § 632.335 hearing) covering 90-day inpatient / 180-day outpatient additional detention criteria and petition/hearing procedures (L. 1980 H.B. 1724 through A.L. 2023 S.B. 106).

headings.title: Appointment of examining physician or licensed psychologist
headings.reviewNote: Requires the court upon respondent request to appoint an available licensed physician or psychologist to examine and testify, excluding program staff or department employees when requested.

headings.title: Continuances restricted to good and sufficient cause
headings.reviewNote: Permits the court to grant continuances only upon a showing of good and sufficient cause.

headings.title: Continued detention pending hearing and thirty-day limit
headings.reviewNote: Provides for continued detention pending hearing unless released on conditions during a continuance, and mandates release if no order is made within 30 days of filing (excluding respondent-requested extensions).

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsection headings for 632.345 (rewrote all 3 shifted/fabricated subsections) covering appointment of an independent physician or licensed psychologist, good-cause continuances, and continued detention pending hearing with 30-day release limit (L. 1980 H.B. 1724 through A.L. 2023 S.B. 106).

headings.title: Conduct of ninety-day inpatient or outpatient hearing
headings.reviewNote: Requires an informal, non-harmful hearing setting for 90-day inpatient or 180-day outpatient petitions in accordance with section 632.335, with due consideration to holding non-jury hearings at the program.

headings.title: Clear and convincing burden of proof on petitioner
headings.reviewNote: Places the burden of proof at the hearing upon the petitioner by clear and convincing evidence.

headings.title: Scope of jury determination and civil procedures
headings.reviewNote: Limits jury instructions and determinations solely to whether the respondent is mentally ill and as a result presents a likelihood of serious harm, with remaining procedures as in civil matters.

headings.title: No requirement for answer or responsive pleading
headings.reviewNote: Provides that the respondent shall not be required to file an answer or other responsive pleading.

headings.title: Ninety-day inpatient or outpatient detention order
headings.reviewNote: Directs the court, upon finding serious harm and program acceptance, to order up to 90 days of inpatient involuntary treatment or up to 180 days of outpatient detention and treatment in the least restrictive environment.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 5 subsection headings for 632.350 (rewrote all 5 shifted/fabricated subsections) covering 90-day inpatient / 180-day outpatient hearing conduct, clear and convincing burden, jury instruction scope, no responsive pleading, and detention order (L. 1980 H.B. 1724 through A.L. 2023 S.B. 106).

headings.title: One-year inpatient or outpatient extension criteria
headings.reviewNote: Permits additional inpatient detention up to one year or outpatient detention up to 180 days at expiration of a 90-day commitment if mental illness and likelihood of serious harm continue and the court so orders after hearing.

headings.title: Petition filing within ninety-day commitment period
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the program head within the 90-day commitment period to file a one-year inpatient or 180-day outpatient petition with an individualized treatment plan following sections 632.330, 632.340, 632.345, and 632.350.

headings.title: One-year inpatient or outpatient detention order
headings.reviewNote: Directs the court, upon finding serious harm and program acceptance, to order up to one year of inpatient involuntary treatment or up to 180 days of outpatient detention and treatment in the least restrictive environment.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsection headings for 632.355 (rewrote all 3 shifted/fabricated subsections) covering one-year inpatient / 180-day outpatient extension authorization, petition filing within the 90-day period, and detention order upon findings (L. 1980 H.B. 1724 through A.L. 2023 S.B. 106).

headings.title: Inpatient facility transfer and notification requirements
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes department to transfer detained persons between facilities and requires written notice to court, guardian, and kin.

headings.title: Transfer to federal agency facilities and restrictions
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes transfer to federal agencies, requires notice, and restricts transfer of persons confined under criminal law.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 632.370 governing inter-facility transfers (including minor-to-adult ward due process hearings and victim notice) and transfers to federal agencies (L. 1980 H.B. 1724 through A.L. 2023 S.B. 106).

headings.title: Mandatory semi-annual evaluation of one-year respondents
headings.reviewNote: Requires semi-annual evaluation of respondents detained for one year and report transmittal to court and counsel.

headings.title: Court hearing on continued detention and dispositions
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes court hearing on continued detention and empowers court to discharge, modify, or remand respondent.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 632.375 establishing 180-day evaluations for one-year respondents and court review hearings with discharge, modification, or remand options (L. 1980 H.B. 1724 through A.L. 2023 S.B. 106).

headings.title: Release to least restrictive environment
headings.reviewNote: Requires release of voluntary or involuntary patients to least restrictive environment with continuing responsibility.

headings.title: Conditional outpatient release for up to one year
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes conditioning release on outpatient care for a period not to exceed one year.

headings.title: Written assumption of responsibility by outpatient facility
headings.reviewNote: Requires receiving facility or agency to agree in writing to assume outpatient responsibility and distribute release conditions.

headings.title: Prescribed trial visits during detention
headings.reviewNote: Permits facility head to authorize short prescribed trial visits outside the facility during detention.

headings.title: Modification of release conditions and inpatient return
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes facility head to modify release conditions, return patient to facility, and request apprehension order.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 5 subsection headings for 632.385 governing release to least restrictive environments, up to one-year conditional outpatient care, written assumption of responsibility, trial visits, and modification/return procedures (L. 1980 H.B. 1724 through A.L. 2023 S.B. 106).

headings.title: Discharge upon recovery or cessation of serious harm
headings.reviewNote: Directs release of involuntarily detained person whenever the person is no longer mentally ill or likelihood of harm ceases.

headings.title: Written notice of early discharge to court
headings.reviewNote: Requires facility head to give written notice to the court whenever a person is discharged prior to order expiration.

headings.title: Cessation of involuntary detention upon voluntary admission
headings.reviewNote: Directs that involuntary detention ceases and court is notified upon good faith voluntary admission under section 632.105.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsection headings for 632.390 governing early release upon recovery or cessation of harm, written court notice, and cessation of involuntary detention upon good-faith voluntary admission (L. 1980 H.B. 1724 through A.L. 2023 S.B. 106).

headings.title: Discharge educational packet and provider information disclosure
headings.reviewNote: Requires provision of educational information packet and permits disclosure of confidential records to care providers.

headings.title: Notice, consent negotiation, and non-consensual disclosure
headings.reviewNote: Establishes notice and consent negotiation procedures and allows release without consent when medically necessary.

headings.title: Definition of care provider
headings.reviewNote: Defines care provider as persons primarily responsible for health care, excluding institutional facility personnel.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsection headings for 632.392 governing discharge educational packets, permissive medically necessary care-provider disclosures, notice/consent negotiation, and care provider definition (L. 1996 S.B. 884 & 841, A.L. 2023 S.B. 106).

headings.title: Involuntary detention and commitment to federal agencies
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes court placement in a federal agency's custody upon a certificate of facility availability, vests the federal facility chief officer with state facility-head powers, and retains Missouri court jurisdiction.

headings.title: Effect of out-of-state federal hospitalization orders
headings.reviewNote: Gives federal hospitalization orders from another state or the District of Columbia the same force and effect in Missouri, recognizes issuing-court retained jurisdiction, and consents to applying the issuing jurisdiction's law to the federal facility chief officer's authority.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 632.395 (rewrote shifted subsection 2) covering court commitment to federal agencies with retained state jurisdiction and recognition of out-of-state or District of Columbia federal hospitalization orders (L. 1980 H.B. 1724, A.L. 2023 S.B. 106).

headings.title: Register of appointed attorneys in probate court
headings.reviewNote: Requires probate judge to prepare and maintain a current register of attorneys available for appointment.

headings.title: Attorney fee allowance and state cost payment
headings.reviewNote: Directs allowance of reasonable attorney fees assessed as costs and paid by state for indigent respondents.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 632.415 governing probate court registers of appointed attorneys and state payment of indigent attorney fees excluding salaried public/publicly funded agency attorneys (L. 1980 H.B. 1724 through A.L. 2023 S.B. 106; cross reference § 631.175).

headings.title: Appeals from court orders and attorney general role
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes expedited appeals under supreme court rules and requires attorney general representation for state.

headings.title: Motion for stay pending appeal and safety exception
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes stay motions but prohibits stays where person presents imminent likelihood of serious physical harm.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 632.430 governing priority expedited appeals with attorney general notice/representation and stays pending appeal with imminent-harm bar (L. 1980 H.B. 1724, A.L. 2023 S.B. 106).

headings.title: Appointment of attorney for all judicial proceedings
headings.reviewNote: Mandates appointment of an attorney for respondent in all judicial proceedings including appeal unless relieved.

headings.title: Mandatory personal contact and consultation timeline
headings.reviewNote: Requires appointed attorney to personally contact respondent within two days and meet in person as soon as possible.

headings.title: Counsel counseling on appeal and post-detention rights
headings.reviewNote: Requires attorney to fully advise respondent of appeal rights and interests if not fully discharged by court.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsection headings for 632.450 establishing mandatory attorney appointment, two-day personal contact deadline, and post-detention appeal counseling (L. 1980 H.B. 1724; cross reference § 631.175).

headings.title: Sheriff apprehension of unauthorized absent patient
headings.reviewNote: Requires sheriff to apprehend and return an unauthorized absent patient upon request of facility head.

headings.title: Conditions authorizing request for patient return
headings.reviewNote: Enumerates five specific circumstances authorizing facility head to request sheriff apprehension of absent patient.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 632.455 governing sheriff apprehension of absent patients and five authorized grounds for requesting return (L. 1982 H.B. 1565 through A.L. 2023 S.B. 106).

headings.title: Continued commitment under pre-1980 sexual psychopath statutes
headings.reviewNote: Provides that persons committed to the department as criminal sexual psychopaths under statutes in effect before August 13, 1980 remain committed under those statutes except as provided in this section.

headings.title: Release application, hearing, probation, and police notice
headings.reviewNote: Permits filing a written release application with the committing court for a hearing leading to at least three years of probation, continued commitment, or post-probation discharge, requiring immediate notice to local law enforcement upon probation or discharge.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 632.475 (rewrote both fabricated subsections) covering continued commitment of criminal sexual psychopaths committed before August 13, 1980, and release applications, hearings, three-year minimum probation or discharge, and law enforcement notice (L. 1980 H.B. 1724, A.L. 1982 S.B. 630; cross reference §§ 589.400 to 589.426).

headings.title: Notice to multidisciplinary team and attorney general
headings.reviewNote: Requires agency with jurisdiction to give written notice regarding sexually violent predators prior to anticipated release.

headings.title: Required notice contents and psychiatric evaluation
headings.reviewNote: Requires the agency with jurisdiction to provide the attorney general and multidisciplinary team with identifying and offense data, institutional/treatment records, and a psychiatrist or psychologist SVP determination.

headings.title: Good-faith immunity for officials and review members
headings.reviewNote: Grants immunity from liability for good-faith conduct without gross negligence to the agency, its employees, multidisciplinary team members, prosecutors' review committee members, and contractors under sections 632.480 to 632.513.

headings.title: Multidisciplinary team establishment and thirty-day assessment
headings.reviewNote: Directs the DMH and DOC directors to establish a multidisciplinary team of up to seven members to review records within thirty days of notice and notify the attorney general of its SVP assessment.

headings.title: Prosecutors' review committee determination and inadmissibility
headings.reviewNote: Directs the prosecutors coordinators training council to appoint a five-member prosecutors' review committee to determine SVP status, making its determination inadmissible as evidence while sharing the multidisciplinary team's assessment.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 5 subsection headings for 632.483 (rewrote shifted/fabricated subsections 2 through 5) covering agency release notice to AG and multidisciplinary team, required records/evaluation contents, good-faith immunity, 7-member multidisciplinary team 30-day assessment, and 5-member prosecutors' review committee determination (L. 1998 H.B. 1405 § 2 through A.L. 2014 S.B. 621).

headings.title: Attorney general petition upon recent overt act
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the attorney general, upon law enforcement notice that a non-custodial sexually violent offender committed a recent overt act, to petition the probate division for up to nine days of detention and evaluation, with notice to the county prosecutor.

headings.title: Court detention and transport order to secure facility
headings.reviewNote: Requires the court, upon determining the person may meet the SVP definition, to order detention and transport to a DMH-designated secure facility, with immediate written AG notice to DMH.

headings.title: Department seven-day evaluation report and extension
headings.reviewNote: Directs DMH to conduct a psychiatrist or psychologist evaluation and submit a written report to the attorney general within seven days of physical custody, with a discretionary 96-hour court extension for good cause.

headings.title: Attorney general petition filing authorization
headings.reviewNote: Requires the attorney general to forward positive DMH evaluations to the prosecutors' review committee for a majority vote within 24 hours and authorizes filing a section 632.486 petition within 48 hours of receiving DMH results.

headings.title: Definition of recent overt act
headings.reviewNote: Defines recent overt act as any act creating reasonable apprehension of harm of a sexually violent nature.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 5 subsection headings for 632.484 (rewrote shifted/fabricated subsections 1 through 3 and tightened subsection 4) covering AG nine-day detention/evaluation petition upon recent overt act, court detention/transport order, DMH seven-day evaluation report and 96-hour extension, prosecutors' review committee 24-hour vote and 48-hour AG petition, and recent overt act definition (L. 1999 H.B. 852 through A.L. 2014 S.B. 621).

headings.title: Ex parte probable cause finding and custody transfer
headings.reviewNote: Directs court to make probable cause finding, order custody, and transfer person to secure facility or county jail.

headings.title: Seventy-two-hour contested probable cause hearing
headings.reviewNote: Requires hearing within seventy-two hours of custody to verify identity and determine probable cause.

headings.title: Procedural rights of respondent at probable cause hearing
headings.reviewNote: Enumerates detainee rights at hearing including counsel, evidence, cross-examination, and record access.

headings.title: Court-ordered evaluation and examination procedures
headings.reviewNote: Directs evaluation by independent psychiatrist or psychologist and sets sixty-day report completion timeline.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 subsection headings for 632.489 governing ex parte probable cause custody transfer, 72-hour contested probable cause hearing, detainee procedural rights, and 60-day court-ordered evaluation (L. 1998 H.B. 1405 § 4 through A.L. 2026 H.B. 2637 & 3155 merged with S.B. 982; severability § 1.1005).

headings.title: Jury trial and unanimous finding requirement
headings.reviewNote: Requires the court or jury to determine SVP status by clear and convincing evidence, mandates a unanimous verdict if tried by a jury, and authorizes appeal.

headings.title: Department custody, secure facility, and treatment
headings.reviewNote: Places committed person in custody of department of mental health for control, care, and treatment until safe.

headings.title: Secure facility housing and segregation from other patients
headings.reviewNote: Requires SVP detainees and committed persons to be housed in a DMH-designated secure facility segregated at all times from other DMH mental health patients, except persons conditionally released under section 632.505.

headings.title: Interagency agreement for housing following probable cause
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes interagency agreement with corrections for post-probable cause confinement with mandatory segregation from offenders.

headings.title: Contract agreements with county jails for confinement
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes department contracts with county jails for confinement with strict separation from jail offenders.

headings.title: Interagency agreement for committed predator care
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes interagency agreement with corrections for care of committed predators with segregation requirements.

headings.title: Contract agreements with health care professionals
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes department contracts with licensed professionals to provide health and mental health care services.

headings.title: Court-directed release upon failure to prove status
headings.reviewNote: Directs release of respondent if court or jury is not satisfied by clear and convincing evidence.

headings.title: Mistrial procedures, secure housing, and retrial deadline
headings.reviewNote: Directs secure holding upon mistrial and mandates retrial within ninety days unless continued under section 632.492.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 9 subsection headings for 632.495 (corrected subsection 1 burden note and rewrote inaccurate subsection 3) covering clear and convincing / unanimous jury finding, DMH commitment, secure facility housing and patient segregation, DOC and county jail agreements, health care contracts, release upon failure of proof, and 90-day mistrial retrial (L. 1998 H.B. 1405 § 6 through A.L. 2026 H.B. 2637 & 3155 merged with S.B. 982; severability § 1.1005).

headings.title: Annual mental examination and court status review
headings.reviewNote: Requires annual mental examination by department and yearly court status review unless conditionally released.

headings.title: Committed person right to petition for release
headings.reviewNote: Preserves person's right to petition court for release and mandates annual written notice and waiver form.

headings.title: Service of petition for conditional release
headings.reviewNote: Requires service of release petition upon committing court, prosecutor, department director, facility, and attorney general.

headings.title: Counsel representation and hearing on petition
headings.reviewNote: Grants right to counsel at hearing and directs trial if court finds by preponderance that person no longer poses harm.

headings.title: Trial procedures, jury right, and burden of proof
headings.reviewNote: Governs release trial rights, jury demand, clear and convincing burden on state, and conditional release order.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 5 subsection headings for 632.498 establishing annual mental examinations and court reviews, right to petition for release with waiver notice, petition service, preponderance hearing with counsel, and clear-and-convincing unanimous jury trial (L. 1998 H.B. 1405 § 7 through A.L. 2013 H.B. 215/374/434/S.B. 188; annotation notes In re Care and Treatment of Coffman).

headings.title: Placement on conditional release and purpose
headings.reviewNote: Directs court to place person on conditional release for outpatient monitoring to prevent condition deterioration.

headings.title: Interagency supervision agreement and release plan
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes interagency agreement with corrections and development of comprehensive conditional release plan.

headings.title: Mandatory statutory conditions of release
headings.reviewNote: Enumerates twenty-one mandatory conditions of release including residence, monitoring, weapons ban, and treatment.

headings.title: Distribution of conditional release order
headings.reviewNote: Requires court to provide copies of conditional release order to person, attorney general, and relevant departments.

headings.title: Continuing department of mental health control and care
headings.reviewNote: Provides that a conditionally released person supervised by a department of corrections probation and parole officer remains under the control, care, and treatment of the department of mental health.

headings.title: Court modification of conditional release conditions
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the court to modify conditions of release on its own motion or upon petition of the department of mental health, the department of corrections, or the person on conditional release.

headings.title: Apprehension and revocation for violation of conditions
headings.reviewNote: Establishes apprehension, emergency revocation, and hearing procedures upon violation of release conditions.

headings.title: Contracts with other agencies for supervision
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes agreements with corrections or other departments and contracts with private entities for supervision.

headings.title: Supervision fees and administrative rulemaking authority
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes collection of supervision fees and subjects rulemaking to chapter 536 nonseverability provisions.

headings.title: Escape notification and criminal escape charges
headings.reviewNote: Directs immediate escape notifications to law enforcement and mandates attorney general filing of escape charges.

headings.title: Local law enforcement access to electronic monitoring
headings.reviewNote: Directs provision of GPS monitoring data and credentials to local law enforcement chief upon request.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 11 subsection headings for 632.505 (rewrote fabricated subsections 5 and 6) covering conditional release placement, DOC interagency supervision plan, 21 mandatory conditions, order distribution, continuing DMH control, condition modification, violation apprehension/revocation, private supervision contracts, fees/nonseverable rulemaking, escape charges, and local police GPS access (L. 2006 H.B. 1698 through A.L. 2013 H.B. 215/374/434/S.B. 188).

headings.title: Attorney general notice obligations to crime victims
headings.reviewNote: Mandates attorney general notice to victims regarding notice, committee determinations, petitions, trials, and escapes.

headings.title: Victim right to attend proceedings and immunity
headings.reviewNote: Guarantees victim right to be present at proceedings and bars causes of action for failure to notify.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 632.507 establishing timely attorney general victim notifications and victim right to attend proceedings with no cause of action for failure to notify (L. 1998 H.B. 1405 § 10 through A.L. 2006 H.B. 1698; effective 6-05-06).

headings.title: Definitions of employee, offender, and secure facility
headings.reviewNote: Defines employee, offender, and secure facility for offenses committed within department facilities.

headings.title: Violence against employee or offender in facility
headings.reviewNote: Establishes class B felony offense for knowingly committing violence to facility employees or fellow offenders.

headings.title: Property damage to department facility or property
headings.reviewNote: Establishes class D felony offense for knowingly damaging buildings or property owned or operated by the department.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 3 subsection headings for 632.520 defining employee, offender, and secure facility and establishing class B felony violence and class D felony property damage penalties (L. 2014 H.B. 1231 merged with S.B. 852 through A.L. 2026 H.B. 2637 & 3155 merged with S.B. 982; severability § 1.1005).

headings.title: Three-year demonstration project for emotionally disturbed children
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes demonstration project in designated county for community-based treatment of severely emotionally disturbed children.

headings.title: Mandatory statutory goals of demonstration project
headings.reviewNote: Enumerates five statutory goals focusing on family preservation, least restrictive care, and replicable service models.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 632.553 establishing a three-year county demonstration project (with 10% county funding and advisory board) and five statutory goals for severely emotionally disturbed children (L. 1989 H.B. 502, et al. § 2).

headings.title: Establishment and composition of governing board
headings.reviewNote: Establishes seven-member governing board appointed by director with advice and consent of mental health commission.

headings.title: Board member terms and expense reimbursement
headings.reviewNote: Provides for three-year board terms, uncompensated service, and reimbursement of necessary expenses.

headings.title: Board responsibilities and quarterly reporting
headings.reviewNote: Tasks board with project implementation, monitoring treatment and cost effectiveness, and quarterly reporting.

headings.title: Department administrative and clerical support
headings.reviewNote: Directs department of mental health to provide clerical and administrative support to the governing board.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 subsection headings for 632.555 establishing the seven-member demonstration project governing board, three-year uncompensated terms, implementation and quarterly reporting duties, and DMH administrative support (L. 1989 H.B. 502, et al. § 3).

headings.title: Definition of mental health care provider
headings.reviewNote: Defines mental health care provider as any person licensed under chapters 334, 335, or 337.

headings.title: Licensure requirement for specified memory therapies
headings.reviewNote: Requires professional licensure to provide repressed memory, recovered memory, reparenting, or multiple personality therapy.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 632.560 defining mental health care provider under chapters 334, 335, or 337 and requiring licensure to provide specified memory, reparenting, or multiple personality therapies (L. 1999 H.B. 343 § 1).

headings.title: Offense of unlawful drone flight over hospital
headings.reviewNote: Defines offense of operating unmanned aircraft within 400 feet vertically over property line or delivering contraband.

headings.title: Measurement of vertical distance from ground level
headings.reviewNote: Specifies that vertical distance extends from ground level for prohibited drone airspace.

headings.title: Definition of mental health hospital
headings.reviewNote: Defines mental health hospital as department facility providing inpatient evaluation, treatment, or care.

headings.title: Authorized operational exceptions to drone prohibition
headings.reviewNote: Enumerates seven exceptions including hospital staff, emergency services, utilities, railroads, and FAA waivers.

headings.title: Warning sign posting requirement and dimensions
headings.reviewNote: Requires conspicuous posting of warning sign measuring at least eleven by fourteen inches at each hospital.

headings.title: Offense grading and felony penalties for contraband
headings.reviewNote: Classifies offense as infraction, elevating to class B, C, or D felony for weapons, escape, or controlled substances.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 6 subsection headings for 632.575 governing unlawful unmanned aircraft operation over mental health hospitals, ground-level vertical distance, hospital definition, seven operational exceptions (footnote notes 'Railway' in original rolls), 11x14-inch warning signage, and infraction/felony grading (L. 2020 H.B. 1963 § 632.460).

headings.title: Authorized petitioners for assisted outpatient treatment
headings.reviewNote: Enumerates five categories of authorized petitioners including program directors, physicians, guardians, and agencies.

headings.title: Venue and probate court jurisdiction for petition
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes petition filing in probate court where respondent is present or reasonably believed to reside.

headings.title: Sworn petition requirements and factual allegations
headings.reviewNote: Requires sworn petition under oath specifying factual grounds, criteria satisfaction, and observer contact information.

headings.title: Exemption from notarization under penalty of perjury
headings.reviewNote: Exempts petitions and supporting affidavits from notarization pursuant to section 492.060 penalty of perjury rules.

headings.title: Prosecution and representation by local prosecutors
headings.reviewNote: Directs prosecuting attorney, county counselor, or circuit attorney to represent petitioner and prosecute petitions.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 5 subsection headings for 632.585 governing assisted outpatient treatment petitioners, probate court venue, sworn factual petition contents, section 492.060 notarization exemption, and local prosecutor representation (L. 2026 H.B. 2637 & 3155; severability § 1.1005).

headings.title: Hearing schedule, counsel appointment, and continuances
headings.reviewNote: Sets hearing within two judicial days, mandates counsel appointment and fees, and limits continuances to good cause.

headings.title: Hearing conduct, procedural rights, and jury request
headings.reviewNote: Requires informal hearing setting and enumerates respondent procedural rights including counsel, evidence, and jury demand.

headings.title: Respondent presence requirement and exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Requires respondent presence unless excused due to physical incapacity or disruptive courtroom conduct.

headings.title: Clear and convincing burden of proof on petitioner
headings.reviewNote: Places burden of proof by clear and convincing evidence upon petitioner throughout hearing.

headings.title: Jury instruction limited to statutory criteria
headings.reviewNote: Restricts jury determination and instructions solely to whether respondent meets assisted outpatient treatment criteria.

headings.title: No requirement for answer or responsive pleading
headings.reviewNote: Provides that respondent is not required to file an answer or other responsive pleading to the petition.

headings.title: Clear and convincing standard for two-year order
headings.reviewNote: Directs court to issue assisted outpatient treatment order for up to two years upon clear and convincing finding.

headings.title: Dismissal of petition upon failure of proof
headings.reviewNote: Directs court to dismiss petition if court or jury does not find clear and convincing evidence of criteria.

headings.title: Mandatory factors for deterioration-based treatment orders
headings.reviewNote: Enumerates ten mandatory factors court or jury must consider before ordering assisted outpatient treatment for deterioration.

headings.title: Consideration of additional relevant factors
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that court or jury may consider any other relevant factors not explicitly enumerated in section.

headings.title: Appointment of independent examining physician or psychologist
headings.reviewNote: Requires court appointment of independent examining professional upon respondent request pursuant to section 632.420.

headings.title: Limited waiver of physician and psychologist privileges
headings.reviewNote: Deems medical and psychologist privileges waived solely for matters directly material and relevant to proceedings.

headings.title: Appeals governed by section 632.430 procedures
headings.reviewNote: Provides that appeals from assisted outpatient treatment orders are governed by section 632.430 expedited procedures.

headings.title: Distinction from inpatient and outpatient detention
headings.reviewNote: Establishes that assisted outpatient treatment is not outpatient detention and excludes general detention rules.

headings.title: Applicability of immunity provisions of section 632.440
headings.reviewNote: Applies statutory civil immunity provisions of section 632.440 to assisted outpatient treatment proceedings.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 15 subsection headings for 632.593 governing assisted outpatient treatment hearing schedule, respondent rights, presence, clear and convincing burden, jury scope, no answer required, up to two-year order, dismissal, ten deterioration factors, additional factors, independent examiner, limited privilege waiver, appeals, detention distinction, and section 632.440 immunity (L. 2026 H.B. 2637 & 3155; severability § 1.1005).

headings.title: Assignment of case manager from behavioral clinic
headings.reviewNote: Directs court to assign a case manager from a certified community behavioral health clinic to each respondent.

headings.title: Ninety-day reporting and immediate noncompliance notice
headings.reviewNote: Requires quarterly court reporting by case manager and respondent and immediate notice of substantial program failure.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 632.595 requiring assignment of a certified community behavioral health clinic case manager and 90-day court reporting with immediate substantial-noncompliance notice (L. 2026 H.B. 2637 & 3155; severability § 1.1005).

headings.title: Order expiration and petition for treatment extension
headings.reviewNote: Provides that treatment orders expire unless an extension petition is filed prior to order expiration.

headings.title: Extension procedures and exclusion of lookback period
headings.reviewNote: Applies original petition procedures to extensions while exempting the thirty-six-month historical lookback requirement.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 2 subsection headings for 632.600 governing expiration of assisted outpatient treatment orders, extension petitions, and exemption from the 36-month lookback period (L. 2026 H.B. 2637 & 3155; severability § 1.1005).

headings.title: Immediate notice of respondent noncompliance to court
headings.reviewNote: Requires treating program or professional to notify court immediately if respondent fails to comply with treatment order.

headings.title: Court evaluation and hospitalization orders without hearing
headings.reviewNote: Empowers court to order community mental health evaluation or hospitalization up to ten or ninety days without hearing.

headings.title: Peace officer transportation and cost reimbursement
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes peace officer transport to facility and provides transportation cost reimbursement under section 632.312.

headings.title: Respondent objection, hearing right, and discharge standard
headings.reviewNote: Provides right to object to non-hearing hospitalization, setting hearing with section 632.593 rights and discharge rules.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked 4 subsection headings for 632.605 establishing immediate noncompliance reporting, court evaluation or hospitalization up to 10 or 90 days without hearing, peace officer transport/reimbursement, and respondent objection hearing with clear and convincing standard (L. 2026 H.B. 2637 & 3155; severability § 1.1005).
